Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at the examples, they all appear to be very similar - essentially the same data just shifted by one day. Let me examine the differences between model forecasts and true outcomes.

Example 1 (2025-06-23):
- Model forecasts are generally higher than true outcomes
- Looking at day 1: model says 73.43, true is 73.27 (model overestimates by ~0.16)
- Day 5: model says 71.70, true is 70.96 (model overestimates by ~0.74)
- Day 9: model says 73.88, true is 72.06 (model overestimates by ~1.82 - this is large!)
- Day 27: model says 77.74, true is 73.08 (model overestimates by ~4.66)

Example 2 (2025-06-19):
- Day 1: model 72.69 vs true 72.74 (model underestimates by -0.05)
- Day 5: model 71.54 vs true 70.96 (model overestimates by +0.58)
- Day 9: model 73.12 vs true 71.93 (model overestimates by +1.19)
- Day 27: model 75.55 vs true 73.08 (model overestimates by +2.47)

Example 3 (2025-06-20):
- Very similar to Example 2
- Day 1: model 73.14 vs true 72.97 (model overestimates by +0.17)
- Day 5: model 71.17 vs true 70.96 (model overestimates by +0.21)
- Day 9: model 73.29 vs true 71.93 (model overestimates by +1.36)


- Day 27: model 75.66 vs true 73.08 (model overestimates by +2.58)

Example 4 (2025-06-18):
- Day 1: model 74.60 vs true 74.61 (model underestimates by -0.01)
- Day 5: model 74.01 vs true 73.54 (model overestimates by +0.47)
